It is not cruel or unreasonable to feel this way. Society places a heavy expectation on siblings to be best friends, but sharing DNA does not automatically guarantee a personality match or a deep connection. The fact that you care about her well-being as a human being shows that you are not coming from a place of malice, but simply a lack of compatibility. It is completely normal to feel closer to your chosen family—your friends—than to a sibling. 

As for "fixing" this, it might help to reframe your expectations. You don't necessarily need to force a deep love or friendship that isn't naturally there. Instead, you can aim for a relationship based on basic respect and cordiality, especially since you are close to your parents and will likely share family spaces. Accepting that it is okay to just be polite acquaintances with your sister can relieve a lot of the guilt and pressure you are carrying.
